facts.heading: Exhausted since October
facts.content: Daniel has been completely burnt out since October. He ended up doing three people's jobs.
facts.evidence: I've been completely burnt out since October. Since October? Did something happen then? Not one thing. We lost a big client, half of our team moved on to the Rescue Plan, so I ended up doing three people's jobs. Just never going back up after that.

facts.heading: Long working day routine
facts.content: Daniel works at a logistics company as a project manager. He stays up late answering messages and thinking about work.
facts.evidence: I'm at my desk by seven and I'm still answering messages at ten at night. Even when I'm not working I'm thinking about work.

facts.heading: Poor sleep quality
facts.content: Daniel's sleep is terrible, and he sleeps about four hours most nights. He wakes up at three in the morning and cannot fall back asleep.
facts.evidence: Most nights I sleep about four hours. I wake up at three in the morning and just can't fall back asleep.

facts.heading: Sleep routine difficulty
facts.content: When Daniel wakes at three in the morning, he has to start work tasks. He looks at the clock and dreads the nights.
facts.evidence: We have to start. Shipping schedules, the client, whether I've forgotten something. And I look at the clock and I do the mountain how little sleep I'm gonna get which makes it worse. Then I lie until about five and get up and make tea. I started dreading the nights, if I'm honest.

facts.heading: Father's Parkinson's diagnosis
facts.content: Daniel's father was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in the autumn. Daniel is involved in his care.
facts.evidence: my father. His diagnosis, Parkinson's disease in the autumn.

facts.heading: Father's current state
facts.content: Daniel's father is mostly himself, but his handshake is slower, he gets frustrated, and he is having a dream and being distraught.
facts.evidence: Still himself, mostly. His handshake is slower, he gets frustrated, he's having a dream and he's always being distraught when.

facts.heading: Driving father to hospital
facts.content: Daniel drives his father to the hospital in Leeds for neurology appointments every few weeks. The journey takes about an hour each way.
facts.evidence: I'm the one who drives him to the hospital in Leeds, neurology appointments are every few weeks, it's about an hour each way.

facts.heading: Care burden on Daniel
facts.content: Daniel is the one who carries the care burden for his father. His younger sister Hannah lives in Toronto.
facts.evidence: Who falls on me? My younger sister Hannah lives in Toronto so all the care for our father who falls on me?

facts.heading: Guilt about expressing feelings
facts.content: Daniel feels guilty for saying anything about his feelings regarding the caregiving.
facts.evidence: Guilty for even saying it.

facts.heading: Father's feelings about tiredness
facts.content: Daniel's father feels selfish to be tired when he is the one who is ill.
facts.evidence: He feels selfish to be tired when he's the one who's ill.

facts.heading: Not telling people about fatigue
facts.content: Daniel does not say anything to anyone about his fatigue. He does not tell his honey eater about how he is feeling.
facts.evidence: So I don't say anything to anyone. Not to a honey eater?

facts.heading: Honey eater's reaction
facts.content: The honey eater asks how Daniel is when he says fine. Daniel believes this is the point where she cannot do anything from Canada.
facts.evidence: She asks how I am when I say fine. would be the point she can't do anything from Canada.

facts.heading: Desired message to convey
facts.content: Daniel wants to convey that he is not fine and that he cannot cope.
facts.evidence: What would she want her to know if you said it? That I'm not fine.

facts.heading: Hospital visit hesitation
facts.content: Daniel hesitates to go into the hospital because he cannot manage the situation.
facts.evidence: That someday I sit in a car park at the hospital for 10 minutes before I go in because I can't

facts.heading: GP visit results
facts.content: Daniel had blood tests which were all normal. The GP said it was stress and exhaustion.
facts.evidence: She had blood tests. They were all normal. She said it's stress and exhaustion.

facts.heading: GP advised no talk therapy
facts.content: The GP said Daniel had not got the time to talk to someone.
facts.evidence: they said I hadn't got the time.

facts.heading: Girlfriend Claire's behavior
facts.content: Claire is very patient and makes tea for Daniel. She is wearing a hoodie.
facts.evidence: She's very patient. She makes me tea and doesn't push me to talk. She's wearing a hoodie too.

facts.heading: Claire stopped asking to go
facts.content: Claire stopped asking Daniel if he wanted to go away for the weekend. Daniel always said no.
facts.evidence: She stopped asking if I want to go away for the weekend because I always said no.

facts.heading: Emails cause hesitation
facts.content: Daniel hesitates to say yes to plans because of emails. He will have to respond to 200 emails if he is away.
facts.evidence: The emails. If I'm away I'll come back to 200 of them.

facts.heading: Rest has a price
facts.content: Daniel feels that even rest has a price. He cannot remember the last time he was brought off.
facts.evidence: So even rest has a price? Can't remember the last time I was brought probably off.

facts.heading: Stopped running activity
facts.content: Daniel stopped running about two months ago. He has not gone back.
facts.evidence: I stopped about two months ago. My legs feel like, like, loud. And I just never went back.

facts.heading: Lost part of self
facts.content: Daniel thinks he has lost a part of himself from stopping running. He recalls running two times a week where nobody could reach him.
facts.evidence: I think I've lost a part of myself. It was two one time in the week, nobody could reach me.

facts.heading: Boss sends late emails
facts.content: Daniel's boss sends emails at 11 at night and expects an answer before breakfast.
facts.evidence: he sends emails at 11 at night and expects an answer before breakfast.

facts.heading: Fear of job loss
facts.content: Daniel is afraid that the company might let him go due to a restructuring in the spring.
facts.evidence: There's a restructuring in the spring and I'm afraid they'll let me go.

facts.heading: Physical symptoms of stress
facts.content: Daniel feels a lot of tiredness and irritability apart from the tiredness.
facts.evidence: A lot mostly. And irritable.

facts.heading: Brief physical incident
facts.content: Daniel slept with a colleague and sat in the toilet for 10 minutes. His hand was shaking while Harry was going by.
facts.evidence: I slept with a colleague last week or in nothing and went and sat in the toilet for 10 minutes. Harry was going and my hand was shaking.

facts.heading: Panic episodes on train
facts.content: Daniel has experienced panic episodes a couple of times. One occurred on a train to Manchester.
facts.evidence: Couple of times. Once on a train to Manchester, just to get off and stand on a platform.

facts.heading: Avoids telling others
facts.content: Daniel had not told anyone about the panic episodes. This included Claire.
facts.evidence: I hadn't told anyone about it, not even Claire.

facts.heading: Coffee consumption habit
facts.content: Daniel drinks about six cups of coffee a day.
facts.evidence: I'm on about six cups a day

facts.heading: Drinks wine in evenings
facts.content: Daniel has started having wine in the evenings to switch his head off.
facts.evidence: I've started having wine in the evenings to switch my head off.

facts.heading: Drinks wine quantity
facts.content: Daniel drinks two to three glasses of wine sometimes.
facts.evidence: Two glasses, sometimes three.

facts.heading: Wine effect duration
facts.content: The wine helps for about an hour. Daniel wakes up anyway.
facts.evidence: Easy. It works for an hour. I wake up three anyway.

facts.heading: Feeling about wine use
facts.content: Daniel does not feel the wine use is helpful. He feels it lists things wrong with him.
facts.evidence: It doesn't feel useful. It feels like I'm listing everything that's wrong with me.

facts.heading: Wants to focus on sleep
facts.content: Daniel thinks he would put the rest down if he could sleep.
facts.evidence: If I could sleep I could probably go put the rest.

facts.heading: Identifies nights as priority
facts.content: Daniel thinks the nights are what he would like to put down first.
facts.evidence: The nights, I think.

facts.heading: Grandfather's coping style
facts.content: Daniel notes his grandfather never complained about anything. He suggests getting on with it.
facts.evidence: He never complained about anything, not once. That's the same. Just get on with it.

facts.heading: Self-perception statement
facts.content: Daniel stated he is not weak but very tired.
facts.evidence: I'm not weak, just very tired.

facts.heading: Belief about self-talk
facts.content: Daniel is unsure if he believes the statement he made about himself yet.
facts.evidence: Maybe, I don't know if I believe it yet.

facts.heading: Proposed small action
facts.content: Daniel agreed to try something small between now and next week.
facts.evidence: Would you be willing to try something small?

facts.heading: Proposed time for action
facts.content: Daniel suggested trying the small action around half past nine in the evening.
facts.evidence: Yeah, half past nine perhaps.

facts.heading: Agreed to meet next week
facts.content: Daniel agreed to meet again next week.
facts.evidence: Yeah, I'll be here.

facts.heading: Worried about train travel
facts.content: Daniel expressed concern about the trains.
facts.evidence: The trains are awful.
